# New Project Scope

## How To Build

A NewProjectScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A NewProjectScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

Creates a new Piton project, with its piton.config.pi set up for Belay and the agents it should write for, and opens it.

### Shape

#### Description

.claude/reference/scope/project:
open-project

.claude/reference/scope/project/open-project:
index.md

use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/application import ApplicationScope
from /scope/project-data import ProjectDataScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/project/open-project import OpenProjectScope
from /ui/components/folder-browser import FolderBrowserScope

    concept: {NewProjectConcept}

concept NewProjectConcept:
    pitch:
        Creates a new Piton project, with its piton.config.pi set up for Belay
        and the agents it should write for, and opens it.

    shape: {NewProjectShape}

shape NewProjectShape:
    description:
        A form titled "New Project", with a close button, holding the project's
        name, where it goes, the template it starts from, and its Belay options,
        and along the bottom a "Cancel" button and a primary "New" button that
        creates it. The name field has focus when the form opens.

    layout:
        The form's body is two columns of equal width side by side, top
        aligned, scrolling together when the panel is too short for them. The
        first holds the project itself: its name, its location, the Git
        checkbox, and the spec, code, and shape roots. The second holds what it
        starts from and what it's written for: the template, then the agents.

    name:
        A "Name" field for the project's name, which is also the name of its
        folder. It can't be empty, contain a slash or backslash, or be "." or
        "..".

    location:
        A "Location" row showing the folder the project's folder goes in, with a

input.command:
cd /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl; mkdir -p spec/scope/import-project; cat > spec/scope/import-project/index.pi <<'EOF'
use /lib
use /ui
from /scope/application import ApplicationScope
from /scope/new-project import NewProjectScope
from /scope/project-data import ProjectDataScope
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/project/open-project import OpenProjectScope
from /ui/components/folder-browser import FolderBrowserScope

export ui-component ImportProjectScope:
    concept: {ImportProjectConcept}

concept ImportProjectConcept:
    pitch:
        Makes an existing folder, such as a codebase that has never had a
        spec, into a Piton project, writing its piton.config.pi set up for
        Belay and the agents it should write for, as a new project's is, and
        opens it, leaving everything already in the folder as it was.

    shape: {ImportProjectShape}

shape ImportProjectShape:
    description:
        A form titled "Import Project", with a close button, laid out as the
        @{NewProjectScope}'s form is, two columns of equal width, and along
        the bottom a "Cancel" button and a primary "Import" button. It holds
        the same fields as a new project's, each looking and checked just as
        it does there, but for where the project is: in place of the Name
        field and the Location row, a "Folder" row, at the top of the first
        column, beneath which come the Git checkbox, the spec, code, and
        shape roots, and, in the second column, the template and the agents.
        The folder's Browse button has focus when the form opens.

    folder:
        A "Folder" row showing the existing folder to import, with a
        "Browse…" button beside it, empty to start with, reading "Choose a
        folder", muted. Browse opens a @{FolderBrowserScope} in place of the
        form, titled "Choose the folder to import", starting in the folder
        holding the open project, or the user's home folder when no project
        is open. Choosing a folder makes it the folder, and choosing or
        cancelling goes back to the form, just as it was left. Beneath the
        row, muted, the folder's full path. The project's name, which names
        its config's anchor as a new project's name does, is the folder's
        name.

        A folder that already holds a piton.config.pi is already a project,
        and can't be imported: the row says so beneath it, with an "Open it
        instead" link that opens it as the @{OpenProjectScope} would and
        closes the form. A folder the user can't write to says that instead.

    defaults:
        Once a folder is chosen, the fields start from what is in it, and
        what has been typed in a field since is kept when another folder is
        chosen. The spec root starts as ./spec. The code root starts as ./src
        where the folder has a src folder, and as ./, the folder itself,
        where it doesn't, since an imported codebase's code is most often all
        of it. The shape root starts as ./spec/shape. "Initialize a Git
        repository" starts checked where the folder isn't in a Git
        repository; where it is, the checkbox is checked, disabled, and reads
        "Already a Git repository". The template and the agents start as a
        new project's do.

        The roots are written and checked as a new project's are, but the
        code root may be ./, the folder itself, holding the spec root, as the
        project's locations allow. A root that already exists in the folder
        is used as it is, and says so beneath its field, muted, "Uses the
        existing folder".

    importing:
        "Import" is disabled, with a tooltip saying why, until a folder that
        can be imported is chosen, the paths are valid, and an agent is
        checked, and while it is importing.

        Pressing it writes the folder's piton.config.pi, just as a new
        project's config is written, named after the folder, with its roots
        and an adapter for each checked agent, and opencode.json as a new
        project writes it, unless there is one. It creates the spec root, the
        code root, and any shape root where they aren't there, and writes the
        chosen template's files into the spec root, each only where no file
        of that name is there already, or an empty index.pi where the
        template gives none and the spec root has no index.pi. It never
        overwrites, moves, renames, or deletes anything already in the
        folder: the folder's own files, its code, and anything already in a
        root are left exactly as they were, and nothing outside the folder
        is touched.

        With "Initialize a Git repository" checked, once the rest is written
        the folder is made a Git repository with `git init`, as a new
        project's is, and nothing is committed. Whether or not Git was just
        initialized, where the folder is in a Git repository, a .gitignore in
        the folder is given the lines ignoring what Suspense keeps for this
        machine alone, as the @{ProjectDataScope} says: written as a new
        project's is where there is none, and where there is one, only the
        lines it lacks are added at its end, beneath a "# Suspense" comment,
        the rest of the file left as it was. If Git fails, the project still
        opens, and a warning notification says the repository couldn't be
        initialized, and why.

        Everything it creates belongs to the user, as the @{ApplicationScope}
        says. Once imported, the project opens as if opened with the
        @{OpenProjectScope}, becoming the @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, and the
        form closes. If anything fails, the form stays open and says what
        went wrong above its buttons, and nothing it wrote before the failure
        is left half done: the piton.config.pi is written last, so a folder
        whose import failed is never taken for a project.
EOF
sed -n 26,36p spec/ui/components/ribbon/project-tab/index.pi; grep -n "project:" -A3 spec/ui/components/ribbon/project-tab/index.pi | head; sed -n 130,138p spec/scope/application/MainWindow.pi; sed -n 96,102p spec/scope/palette/index.pi

content.text:
I added an Import Project feature to the spec: it makes an existing folder into a project, with the same agent, template and root choices as New Project. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` wrote 80 files, and the new page is at `.claude/reference/scope/import-project/index.md`.

## What changed in the spec

**1. New Import Project form** (`spec/scope/import-project/index.pi`)
- **`#description`:** an "Import Project" form laid out like New Project. The Name and Location fields are replaced by a single "Folder" row. Everything else is the same: the Git checkbox, spec/code/shape roots, template and agents. The buttons are Cancel and Import.
- **`#folder`:**
  - Browse opens the folder browser, titled "Choose the folder to import".
  - The project is named after the folder.
  - A folder that already has a `piton.config.pi` is refused, with an "Open it instead" link.
  - A folder you can't write to says so.
- **`#defaults`:**
  - The spec root starts as `./spec`.
  - The code root starts as `./src` if that folder exists, otherwise `./`, meaning the whole folder.
